 San Jose, CA / Storyteller / Nov 11, 2026 /
 With the rainy season already underway, Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists is encouraging San Jose homeowners to plan new tree plantings now, during the best planting window of the year. The family-run company has cared for South Bay trees since 1995 and is sharing tips to help homeowners choose trees that thrive and stand the test of time, while also boosting their properties’ curb appeal.
 A Local Lesson in Choosing the Right Tree 
 In late August, the city of San Jose tagged 35 dead or dying trees along the Zanker Road median for removal. The trees, which included loquats, purple leaf plums, and European olives, weren’t suited to the growing conditions of a busy street median or to San Jose’s drought conditions. The city plans to replace them with 100 trees better suited to the area.
 The same principle applies at home. A tree planted in the wrong spot, or one that needs more water than the local climate provides, is more likely to struggle, decline, and eventually require removal.
 Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists Why Fall and Winter Are the Best Time to Plant 
 Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists recommends planting in fall for California homeowners. Cooler temperatures ease the stress on young trees, and winter rain soaks the soil, so roots have months to spread before summer heat hits.
 “A tree is a long-term investment, and most problems we see start on planting day,” said Doug Anderson, owner of Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists. “Picking the right species for the right spot, and planting it while the rains can help, gives a new tree the best start it can get.”
 How to Pick Trees That Last
 Anderson’s arborists recommend weighing these factors before planting:
 Space to grow: Trees planted in tight spaces can have stunted growth and become more vulnerable to disease. A tree planted too close to a structure can also cause conflicts with belowground infrastructure.
 Sunlight: Different species need different amounts of light, so match the tree to the sun patterns on your property.
 Soil: A soil test identifies nutrient deficiencies and acidity levels, which helps determine which species will thrive.
 Water needs : Trees suited to San Jose’s climate need less irrigation once established.
 Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists Trees That Do Well in San Jose 
 Arborists use the USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map, as well as regional data, to choose species that can handle local conditions. Good options for San Jose include blue oak, a slow-growing native that needs little water once established; western redbud, a California native that tolerates full sun and low water; and desert willow, a drought-tolerant small tree with trumpet-shaped summer flowers.
 Tree Planting in San Jose 
 Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists offers tree planting and transplanting in San Jose for homes and businesses. Its arborists help with every step, from selecting species suited to the local climate to caring for young trees as they mature. The company serves property owners across San Jose, Sunnyvale , and Santa Clara County.
 Property owners can schedule a free estimate by calling 408-226-8733.
 About Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists 
 Anderson’s Tree Care Specialists is a local, family-run tree care company founded in San Jose in 1995. The company serves homeowners and businesses across San Jose and Santa Clara County with ISA certified arborists on staff, including arborists who hold the ISA Tree Risk Assessment Qualification. Anderson’s is accredited by the Tree Care Industry Association and is a member of the International Society of Arboriculture and the American Society of Consulting Arborists. Services include tree risk assessment, pruning, removal, stump removal, tree planting, plant health care, and 24/7 emergency response. The company is fully licensed, bonded, and insured (California Contractor License No. 705171). Learn more at andersonstreecare.com .
